sentences.en: Today, when a man attacked an Iraqi restaurant in Portland, Oregon, it felt to the owner like an attack on his country, an act of hate.
sentences.zh: 今天，当一名男子袭击了俄勒冈州波特兰的一家伊拉克餐厅时，店主觉得这就像是对他国家的袭击，是一次仇恨犯罪。

sentences.en: But as details emerged about the man who did it, the story became far more complicated.
sentences.zh: 但随着肇事者细节的浮现，这个故事变得远比想象中复杂。

sentences.en: It's Friday, November 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月3日，星期五。

sentences.en: Dave, describe for me what we see on the surveillance video from this restaurant, Dar Salaam, on the night of April 25th.
sentences.zh: 戴夫，请向我描述一下我们在4月25日晚这家名为Dar Salaam的餐厅的监控视频中看到了什么。

sentences.en: It's a busy night at the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 那是餐厅里生意兴隆的一个晚上。

sentences.en: And you can see on the surveillance video that a man with a shaved head walks in with a friend and takes a seat in the middle of the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 你可以从监控视频中看到，一个剃着光头的男子和朋友走了进来，在餐厅中间找了个座位坐下。

sentences.en: People around him are all eating.
sentences.zh: 他周围的人都在吃东西。

sentences.en: And he doesn't order.
sentences.zh: 而他没有点餐。

sentences.en: He sits there.
sentences.zh: 他就坐在那里。

sentences.en: He looks around at photos of Iraq that are covering the walls.
sentences.zh: 他环顾四周，看着贴满墙壁的伊拉克照片。

sentences.en: Dave Phillips has been reporting on what happened that night.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·菲利普斯一直在报道那天晚上发生的事情。

sentences.en: You see the waiter come up and ask again and again if they can help him.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到服务员走过来，一次又一次地问是否需要帮忙。

sentences.en: And then after about a half hour, he and his friend get up and the man with the shaved head is looking around, trying to
sentences.zh: 大约半小时后，他和朋友站了起来，那个光头男子四处张望，试图

sentences.en: leave, maybe a little nervous, his hands jammed in his pockets.
sentences.zh: 离开，可能有点紧张，双手插在口袋里。

sentences.en: And then really without warning, he picks up a chair.
sentences.zh: 接着，毫无征兆地，他拿起了一把椅子。

sentences.en: You can see him slightly test it for weight.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他微微试了试椅子的重量。

sentences.en: And he swings it as hard as he can into the waiter's head.
sentences.zh: 然后他用尽全力把椅子砸向服务员的头部。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: A customer goes on the attack at an Iraqi restaurant in North Portland.
sentences.zh: 一名顾客在波特兰北部的一家伊拉克餐厅发动袭击。

sentences.en: An employee was hit over the head with a chair.
sentences.zh: 一名员工被椅子砸中了头部。

sentences.en: The owners of Dar Salaam say two men were in the restaurant for about an hour, at times yelling racial slurs at staff.
sentences.zh: Dar Salaam的店主说，两名男子在餐厅里呆了一个小时左右，期间对员工大喊种族歧视的侮辱性词汇。

sentences.en: When one seen on the right picks up a chair and hits a waiter so hard, it left the server with a bruised shoulder.
sentences.zh: 当右边看到的这个人拿起椅子砸向服务员时，力道之大，导致这名服务员的肩膀都淤青了。

sentences.en: After what happens in the restaurant, right away, Jay Zaheb, the owner of the restaurant, gets a call from his sister saying, you've got to come down, there's been an attack.
sentences.zh: 餐厅发生事情后不久，餐厅老板杰·萨希布就接到了姐姐的电话，说你得赶紧过来，出事了。

sentences.en: I get a phone call from my sister and cry and yelling, screaming to me, Jay, somebody attacked us.
sentences.zh: 我接到我姐姐的电话，在哭，在喊，对我尖叫，杰，有人袭击了我们。

sentences.en: He rushes down.
sentences.zh: 他赶了过去。

sentences.en: I left my car like running, you know, the doors open.
sentences.zh: 我的车都还没熄火，你知道的，车门还开着。

sentences.en: In the parking lot?
sentences.zh: 在停车场里？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was really worried.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时真的很担心。

sentences.en: And then when I get close to the restaurant, I say, like, tables are broken, glasses everywhere, police everywhere.
sentences.zh: 当我靠近餐厅时，我看到，桌子碎了，到处都是玻璃，到处都是警察。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And I really, I didn't understand what happened that night.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我真的不明白那天晚上发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, Dave, take me through what unfolds after that from a legal perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以，戴夫，带我了解一下之后从法律角度看是如何发展的。

sentences.en: Well, so what's really tricky is that the man with the shaved head didn't just hit an Iraqi waiter with a chair.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最棘手的是，那个光头男子不只是用椅子打了一个伊拉克服务员。

sentences.en: He hit an Iraqi waiter with a chair in Portland, Oregon in 2017, right when the city is completely on edge over what it sees as a rise in white nationalism and hate crimes.
sentences.zh: 他在2017年的俄勒冈州波特兰用椅子打了一个伊拉克服务员，当时这座城市正因为白人至上主义和仇恨犯罪的增加而极度神经紧绷。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, someone spray-painted ISIS on a mosque in North Portland.
sentences.zh: 就在周末，有人在波特兰北部的一座清真寺上喷上了“ISIS”的涂鸦。

sentences.en: Students and teachers have found swastikas and other racial slurs written inside the building.
sentences.zh: 学生和老师在建筑内部发现了纳粹万字旗和其他种族侮辱词汇。

sentences.en: were killed by knife attack on a Portland train Friday after coming to the aid of two women who appeared to be Muslim.
sentences.zh: 周五，在波特兰的一辆火车上，两名女子疑似为穆斯林，有人挺身而出帮助她们，却不幸被持刀袭击身亡。

sentences.en: And so they really wanted to make a stand and say, hey, we are Portlandia.
sentences.zh: 所以他们真的很想表明立场，说，嘿，我们是波特兰人。

sentences.en: We're this really eclectic, creative city.
sentences.zh: 我们是一座非常多元、富有创造力的城市。

sentences.en: And I think local prosecutors really wanted to show that they weren't going to stand for something like this.
sentences.zh: 我认为当地检察官真的很想表明他们不会容忍这样的事情发生。

sentences.en: And what happens is they increased the charges on him from misdemeanor charges where he probably would have gotten probation to a hate crime,
sentences.zh: 结果就是，他们将对他的指控从原本可能判处缓刑的轻罪升级为仇恨犯罪，

sentences.en: essentially a bias-related crime and felony level assault.
sentences.zh: 本质上是偏见相关犯罪和重罪级别的袭击。

sentences.en: My experience, eight years or nine years in Portland, we didn't have this kind of things.
sentences.zh: 以我在波特兰八九年的经历，我们从未有过这种事。

sentences.en: And I really be honest with you, I, this guy, what he did, brings so much memory to me and to my family.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这个家伙做的事，勾起了我和我家人太多的回忆。

sentences.en: And I don't know, I really, after the incident happens often now, really, I don't feel safe again.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，真的，自从那次事件发生后，现在我真的再也感觉不到安全了。

sentences.en: The owner of the restaurant, what happened really unnerves him, because basically what he had been
sentences.zh: 餐厅老板对发生的事情感到非常不安，因为基本上他多年来一直在

sentences.en: running away from for years had suddenly come right into the middle of his life again.
sentences.zh: 逃避的东西突然又重新回到了他的生活正中央。

sentences.en: I grew up and raised in Baghdad, and always we hear about war.
sentences.zh: 我在巴格达长大，我们听到的总是关于战争的事。

sentences.en: So he had been a middle-class kid, a college kid, actually, going to business school in Baghdad when the Iraq war started.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克战争爆发时，他还是个中产阶级孩子，实际上是在巴格达读商学院的大学生。

sentences.en: My fellow citizens, at this hour, American and coalition forces are in the early stages of military operations to disarm Iraq, to free its people.
sentences.zh: 我的同胞们，此时此刻，美国和联盟部队正处于解除伊拉克武装、解放其人民的军事行动初期。

sentences.en: Baghdad tonight, under heavy bombardment on the day the war started.
sentences.zh: 战争爆发的那天晚上，巴格达遭到了猛烈的轰炸。

sentences.en: American and British troops are in action on land, sea, and in the air.
sentences.zh: 美英军队在陆地、海洋和空中展开行动。

sentences.en: And he was actually kind of excited about the US invasion because he thought it would be liberation.
sentences.zh: 其实他当时对美军入侵还有点兴奋，因为他以为那是解放。

sentences.en: He thought that lives would get better for everyone, and so did his family.
sentences.zh: 他以为每个人的生活都会变好，他的家人也是这么想的。

sentences.en: But they quickly realized that it didn't.
sentences.zh: 但他们很快发现事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Order melted away.
sentences.zh: 秩序荡然无存。

sentences.en: There was no authority to replace the Ba'athists that had been driven out.
sentences.zh: 没有任何权威来取代被赶走的复兴党人。

sentences.en: And so very quickly it turned into first looting and then killing.
sentences.zh: 所以很快情况就演变成先是抢劫，然后是杀戮。

sentences.en: You see things you don't want to see it, like armies and shooting and killing, kidnapping,
sentences.zh: 你看到了你不想看到的东西，比如军队、枪击、杀戮、绑架、

sentences.en: bombing.
sentences.zh: 轰炸。

sentences.en: Weekly, you know, we hear this kind of news.
sentences.zh: 每周，你知道的，我们都会听到这种新闻。

sentences.en: And even the day when I want to go, like, to the college or do something or go to work, and always I hug my mom, I hug my dad, say, you know,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我想要去，比如去大学、做点什么或者去上班的日子里，我总是拥抱我妈妈，拥抱我爸爸，说，你知道的，

sentences.en: pray for me.
sentences.zh: 为我祈祷。

sentences.en: I don't know if I'll see you again or not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我还能不能再见到你。

sentences.en: So piece by piece, the Sahib family's life starts falling apart, and they have to move from their neighborhood and their jobs disappear.
sentences.zh: 就这样，萨希布一家的生活一点点开始崩塌，他们不得不搬离自己的社区，工作也消失了。

sentences.en: But they're trying to hold it together.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍在努力维持生活。

sentences.en: Jaith is still going to school.
sentences.zh: 杰斯还在上学。

sentences.en: They're still living in Baghdad until this one day when he's on his way to class and everything for him falls apart.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然住在巴格达，直到有一天他在去上课的路上，他的一切都崩溃了。

sentences.en: My college is far from my home, about like 15 minutes drive.
sentences.zh: 我的大学离我家很远，开车大约15分钟。

sentences.en: So, you know, I left home and I had breakfast and I want to go to the college.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我离开家吃过早饭，想要去大学。

sentences.en: And then when I was driving, I was very close, like five minutes far from the college.
sentences.zh: 当我开车时，已经很近了，离大学只有大约五分钟的车程。

sentences.en: And then just, I saw like lighting and big exploding and noise everywhere.
sentences.zh: 然后突然，我看到像闪电一样的光、大爆炸和到处都是噪音。

sentences.en: And then after that, I don't know what happens.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我什么都不知道了。

sentences.en: Three weeks later,
sentences.zh: 三个星期后，

sentences.en: I found out I was in the car bomb.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在汽车炸弹事件中受伤。

sentences.en: When I wake from the coma after three weeks, I can't eat, I can't talk.
sentences.zh: 三周后从昏迷中醒来时，我吃不下饭，也说不出话。

sentences.en: I was very skinny.
sentences.zh: 我非常消瘦。

sentences.en: After I left the hospital, it takes me about two months.
sentences.zh: 离开医院后，我花了大约两个月时间。

sentences.en: I was just home.
sentences.zh: 我只是呆在家里。

sentences.en: He falls into this depression where he doesn't want to leave the house.
sentences.zh: 他陷入了一种不愿出门的抑郁状态。

sentences.en: He doesn't know what to do with his life.
sentences.zh: 他不知道该拿自己的人生怎么办。

sentences.en: He's both fearful and filled with, I guess, dread, you know, that there's nothing left for him anymore.
sentences.zh: 他既恐惧又充满，我想，担忧，你知道的，觉得他再也没有剩下什么了。

sentences.en: I just feel like, really, I don't want to live again.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，真的，我不想再活下去了。

sentences.en: And I think in a big way, that's why he felt he had to leave Iraq, is that everything in Iraq was traumatic to him.
sentences.zh: 我认为很大程度上，这就是为什么他觉得自己必须离开伊拉克，因为伊拉克的一切对他的都是一种创伤。

sentences.en: It all reminded him of the loss and the death that he'd experienced.
sentences.zh: 这一切都让他想起了他所经历的失去与死亡。

sentences.en: I left Iraq, I went to Syria.
sentences.zh: 我离开了伊拉克，去了叙利亚。

sentences.en: And after Syria, I went to India.
sentences.zh: 离开叙利亚后，我去了印度。

sentences.en: And after India, I went to Europe.
sentences.zh: 离开印度后，我去了欧洲。

sentences.en: Jace leaves Iraq, assuming he'll never come back.
sentences.zh: 杰斯离开伊拉克时，以为自己再也不会回来了。

sentences.en: And he goes to, I think, six countries and accidentally meets his wife, who is from a place that he's never heard of, Portland, Oregon.
sentences.zh: 他去了，我想有六个国家，然后意外地遇到了他的妻子，妻子来自一个他从未听说过的地方——俄勒冈州波特兰。

sentences.en: And they get married and move to the United States together.
sentences.zh: 他们结婚并一起搬到了美国。

sentences.en: I think that the United States is probably one of the last places that Jace wanted to end up because he was kind of afraid of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国可能是杰斯最不想去的地方之一，因为他有点害怕这个国家。

sentences.en: The United
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: States had invaded his country.
sentences.zh: 入侵了他的国家。

sentences.en: And so when he ended up here, I think he thought that Americans were much different, much more pro-war, much more anti-Iraq.
sentences.zh: 所以当他最终来到这里时，我想他以为美国人会很不一样，更加好战，更加反伊拉克。

sentences.en: That time, somebody asked me, say, from Middle East, and I don't mention from Iraq.
sentences.zh: 那时候，有人问我，说我来自中东，我没有提我来自伊拉克。

sentences.en: And they asked me, OK, where are the Middle East?
sentences.zh: 他们问我，好吧，中东在哪里？

sentences.en: And I don't answer those questions.
sentences.zh: 我没有回答那些问题。

sentences.en: I'm not just Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 我不仅仅代表中东。

sentences.en: And so at first, he was very hesitant to even say that he was Iraqi.
sentences.zh: 所以起初，他甚至很不愿说自己是伊拉克人。

sentences.en: And then it takes time.
sentences.zh: 这需要时间。

sentences.en: And then after six months, seven months, start more open, you know, for people.
sentences.zh: 六七个月后，开始对人们更加敞开心扉，你知道的。

sentences.en: And I start, you know, talk about Iraq.
sentences.zh: 我开始，你知道的，谈论伊拉克。

sentences.en: And I saw people accept that from me.
sentences.zh: 我看到人们接受了我这一点。

sentences.en: And they start asking me questions about my family.
sentences.zh: 他们开始问我关于我家人的问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, so I start to feel really welcome here.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，所以我开始觉得在这里真的很受欢迎。

sentences.en: And the story starts from there.
sentences.zh: 故事就是从这里开始的。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: It's an exotic flavor you don't find very often in the States.
sentences.zh: 这是一种你在美国不常能找到的异国风味。

sentences.en: And the family behind the counter is just as unique as the dishes they serve.
sentences.zh: 柜台后面的这一家人和他们端出的菜肴一样独特。

sentences.en: Jade Saheb stands next to his mother, cooking up some of their favorite dishes.
sentences.zh: 杰·萨希布站在母亲身旁，烹制着他们最喜爱的一些菜肴。

sentences.en: So in the beginning, it was hard.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始，这很难。

sentences.en: But I was having really joy working, you know.
sentences.zh: 但我工作时真的很开心，你知道的。

sentences.en: Now, you guys.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们看。

sentences.en: Now, it's really good.
sentences.zh: 现在，真的很好。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Their restaurant is an old carriage house.
sentences.zh: 他们的餐厅是一栋老马车房。

sentences.en: And they've completely redecorated it.
sentences.zh: 他们把这里重新装修了一番。

sentences.en: It's very brightly painted yellow and red walls.
sentences.zh: 墙壁刷成了非常明亮的黄色和红色。

sentences.en: And they've covered all of the walls with different photographs.
sentences.zh: 他们用各种照片贴满了所有的墙壁。

sentences.en: Photographs of Baghdad during the war, but also ancient art, paintings.
sentences.zh: 有战争期间巴格达的照片，也有古代艺术品和绘画。

sentences.en: It's basically like a showcase for a scrapbook of Iraqi culture.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像是伊拉克文化的剪贴簿展览馆。

sentences.en: So I just kind of try to, you know, educate people about Iraq and the culture too.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想，你知道的，让人们了解伊拉克及其文化。

sentences.en: And I feel like confusing because I left 2006 because I don't like my country anymore.
sentences.zh: 我感到很纠结，因为我在2006年离开是因为我不再喜欢我的国家了。

sentences.en: But still some part of me is missing it.
sentences.zh: 但内心深处仍然有些部分在想念它。

sentences.en: Always when I come to the restaurant, I feel like I'm going to really to Iraq.
sentences.zh: 每当我来到餐厅，我都觉得我真的回到了伊拉克。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That you've, that you've created a, a part of Iraq in your restaurant, but it's a, but it's on your own terms and it's, and it's peaceful.
sentences.zh: 你在餐厅里创造了，创造了一个伊拉克的缩影，但这是，但这是按你自己的方式创造的，而且是，而且是和平的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The name of the restaurant called Dar Salaam.
sentences.zh: 这家餐厅的名字叫Dar Salaam。

sentences.en: It's Arabic word and in English it means the house of peace.
sentences.zh: 这是一个阿拉伯语词汇，在英语中它的意思是“和平之家”。

sentences.en: The house of peace.
sentences.zh: 和平之家。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then on a busy night, this guy with a shaved head walks in, takes a seat against the wall.
sentences.zh: 然后在一个繁忙的夜晚，一个剃着光头的家伙走了进来，在靠墙的座位坐下。

sentences.en: And after a couple of minutes attacks one of his waiters.
sentences.zh: 过了几分钟后，他袭击了他的一名服务员。

sentences.en: And I think that having this man with a shaved head come into the restaurant and, and do something like this really brought
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个剃着光头的男人来到餐厅，并且做出这样的举动，真的让

sentences.en: the war back in this, this vivid way for him that really unsettled him much more than just a simple assault would.
sentences.zh: 战争以这种生动的方式重新浮现在他脑海中，这让他感到的不安，远超一次简单的袭击。

sentences.en: From that night, I don't feel safe anymore.
sentences.zh: 从那天晚上起，我再也没有安全感了。

sentences.en: Like before I like to walk, you know, at, at night, you know, sometime, you know, close to my business, you know, I feel safe.
sentences.zh: 就像以前我喜欢散步，你知道的，在晚上，有时候，你知道的，在我的店附近，你知道的，我觉得很安全。

sentences.en: Like I can, but now I don't feel safe anymore.
sentences.zh: 就像我以前那样，但现在我不再觉得安全了。

sentences.en: I feel scared.
sentences.zh: 我觉得害怕。

sentences.en: Like maybe some, I will get hit.
sentences.zh: 总觉得也许某个人，我会挨打。

sentences.en: Somebody will attack me always, you know.
sentences.zh: 总有人会袭击我，你知道的。

sentences.en: You're, you're looking over your shoulder.
sentences.zh: 你总是会提心吊胆、环顾四周。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Really.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: That's, that's, that's exactly what I feel.
sentences.zh: 这就是我内心的真实感受。

sentences.en: It brought the war back and, and raised the question for him that he might never be able to get away from it.
sentences.zh: 这唤醒了战争的回忆，并给他提出了一个问题：他可能永远无法摆脱这段阴影。

sentences.en: I just want to find a reason why he did this to my employee and to my sister and to my customer.
sentences.zh: 我只想找出原因，为什么他要对我的员工、我的妹妹和我的顾客做出这种事。

sentences.en: I just, I, I just want to find the answer.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我只想找到答案。

sentences.en: So that's where it gets kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 事情就是从这里开始变得有点意思了。

sentences.en: The man, you know, he, he's wearing a hoodie, he's muscular, he's got a shaved head.
sentences.zh: 这个人，你知道的，他穿着一件连帽衫，身材健硕，留着光头。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people at the restaurant might've thought that he was some, some skinhead essentially.
sentences.zh: 我想餐厅里的很多人可能都会觉得他基本上是个极端分子。

sentences.en: Uh, in fact, he's a career sergeant major in the United
sentences.zh: 呃，事实上，他是美国

sentences.en: States Marine Corps, uh, a 40 year old guy named Damian Rodriguez who had done four deployments to
sentences.zh: 海军陆战队的一名资深上士，呃，一个40岁的家伙，名叫达米安·罗德里格斯，曾四次被部署到

sentences.en: Iraq and Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克和阿富汗。

sentences.en: And that's what really caught my attention.
sentences.zh: 而这正是真正吸引我注意的地方。

sentences.en: Here's this guy with this long history of, of exposure to combat coming into an Iraqi restaurant and attacking the waiter.
sentences.zh: 这样一个有着长期战场经历的人，竟然来到一家伊拉克餐厅袭击服务员。

sentences.en: To what extent was this a hate crime?
sentences.zh: 这在多大程度上是一起仇恨犯罪？

sentences.en: And to what extent was it a wound of war?
sentences.zh: 又在多大程度上是战争创伤？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the times to access all of the reporting, but what if you could explore the times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅时报才能阅读所有报道，但如果你能免费体验时报一个月而无需提供信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free a month to go behind the paywall to see what time subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载纽约时报应用时，你在该应用里的第一个月是免费的——有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York times, download the times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅纽约时报，今天就下载时报应用，享受30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: After I saw the news that this Marine sergeant major had attacked the restaurant, I started calling around because I wanted
sentences.zh: 在我看到这位海军陆战队上士袭击餐馆的新闻后，我开始四处打听，因为我想

sentences.en: to know not what had happened that night that had already been covered, but what had happened in his life in all the years leading up to it.
sentences.zh: 知道的不是那天晚上发生了什么——那些已经报道过了，而是他在此之前的所有岁月里生活经历了什么。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: My name is Robbie Bellow, and I'm the mother of Sergeant Major Damien Rodriguez.
sentences.zh: 我叫罗比·贝洛，我是达米安·罗德里格斯上士的母亲。

sentences.en: I want to ask you just about Damien as a young kid.
sentences.zh: 我想问问你关于达米安小时候的事。

sentences.en: Just give me a feeling for kind of for
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲

sentences.en: Damien himself as a young boy.
sentences.zh: 达米安小时候是个什么样的男孩吗。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But when they were very little, I played Perry Como songs.
sentences.zh: 但当他们还很小的时候，我播放佩里·科莫的歌曲。

sentences.en: My mother was a voice teacher, so we were always trying to get Damien to sing.
sentences.zh: 我母亲是一名声乐老师，所以我们总是试图让达米安唱歌。

sentences.en: And he just hated that.
sentences.zh: 但他就是讨厌那样。

sentences.en: He didn't want to sing in front of anybody.
sentences.zh: 他不想在任何人面前唱歌。

sentences.en: And then one time he said, OK, to please grandma or whatever.
sentences.zh: 然后有一次他说，好吧，为了让奶奶高兴或者别的什么。

sentences.en: And then we couldn't get him to stop.
sentences.zh: 结果我们就没办法让他停下来了。

sentences.en: It was so funny.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: He kept on singing.
sentences.zh: 他一直唱个不停。

sentences.en: Then the other thing that always struck me was that my dad being from World War II, it was very important to put the flag out on holidays.
sentences.zh: 然后另一件让我印象深刻的事是，我父亲经历过二战，在节日里插上国旗非常重要。

sentences.en: And Damien was so excited to do the salute and stand with my dad.
sentences.zh: 达米安非常兴奋能跟我父亲一起敬礼和站岗。

sentences.en: And he would always try to dress up very formal.
sentences.zh: 他总是试着穿得很正式。

sentences.en: He started dressing up as a Marine when he was eight years old.
sentences.zh: 他八岁的时候就开始把自己打扮成海军陆战队的模样。

sentences.en: He put the black stuff on his face that they put on so you're not seen in the dark.
sentences.zh: 他把那种黑色的伪装油涂在脸上，这样在黑暗中就不会被看见。

sentences.en: And like under his eyes?
sentences.zh: 就像眼睛下面那种？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And of course, every Halloween, he was dressed up as a Marine.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个万圣节，他都打扮成海军陆战队员。

sentences.en: I think if you asked him who he was and to describe himself, he would just say that he was a Marine.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你问他是谁、让他描述自己，他会直接说自己是一名海军陆战队员。

sentences.en: He tried to sign up even before he was old enough.
sentences.zh: 他甚至在年龄还没到时就试图报名入伍。

sentences.en: And then he got his GED so that he could enlist earlier and didn't have to finish high school.
sentences.zh: 后来他考取了高中同等学历证书（GED），以便能更早入伍，而不必读完高中。

sentences.en: I think it's a place where he found himself.
sentences.zh: 我想这是他找到自我归属的地方。

sentences.en: He enjoyed the challenge and the mission and serving his country and talking to people who served with him.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢挑战、任务、为国家服务，以及和与他并肩作战的人聊天。

sentences.en: They, across the board, loved him.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人，无一例外都很喜欢他。

sentences.en: He was our platoon sergeant.
sentences.zh: 他是我们的排长。

sentences.en: So he was in charge of all of us.
sentences.zh: 所以他负责管理我们所有人。

sentences.en: Jimmy Gentile served under Rodriguez in the Marines.
sentences.zh: 吉米·詹蒂莱曾在罗德里格斯手下的海军陆战队服役。

sentences.en: You know, I look back on it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我回想起来。

sentences.en: It's more like he was babysitting a lot of us because we were all so young.
sentences.zh: 与其说他是我们的长官，不如说他更像是在照顾我们这群年轻人，因为我们当时都太年轻了。

sentences.en: How young were you?
sentences.zh: 你们有多年轻？

sentences.en: I was 20.
sentences.zh: 我当时20岁。

sentences.en: And then we had guys in the platoon that were 17, 18 years old.
sentences.zh: 我们排里还有17、18岁的孩子。

sentences.en: He did four combat tours, two in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 他执行过四次战斗任务，其中两次在伊拉克。

sentences.en: But really what stuck with him, what he was never able to move beyond was a single day back in his first tour in Ramadi, Iraq.
sentences.zh: 但真正深深刻在他脑海中、让他永远无法释怀的，是他在伊拉克拉马迪第一次执行任务时的一天。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的。

sentences.en: This is March 16th of 2004.
And this is handwritten just before things happened.
sentences.zh: 这是在事情发生前不久手写的。

sentences.en: So he said to the family, how's everyone doing?
sentences.zh: 他对家人说，大家过得怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm doing pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我过得挺好的。

sentences.en: Sorry, I haven't written sooner, but it's been real busy.
sentences.zh: 抱歉没早点写信，因为实在太忙了。

sentences.en: Kuwait was boring, but here in our Ramadi, I'm trying to read his writing.
sentences.zh: 科威特很无聊，但在我们拉马迪这里，我试着辨认他的字迹。

sentences.en: It's a different story.
sentences.zh: 这是完全不同的情况。

sentences.en: It's a city with a lot of bad guys that are already out and about.
sentences.zh: 这是一个到处都是到处乱晃的坏蛋的城市。

sentences.en: So this is right when the war in Iraq is starting to come off the wheels, when American troops are
sentences.zh: 所以正是在这个时候，伊拉克战争开始失控，美国部队

sentences.en: starting to realize that the insurgency is something bigger and more organized than they thought.
sentences.zh: 开始意识到叛乱分子的规模比他们想象的要大、组织得也更严密。

sentences.en: And so we're doing a lot more patrols now than we did before.
sentences.zh: 因此我们现在执行的巡逻任务比以前多得多。

sentences.en: Yesterday on patrol, we had about
sentences.zh: 昨天在巡逻时，我们有大约

sentences.en: 100 kids following us.
sentences.zh: 100个孩子跟在我们后面。

sentences.en: Well, things are going good.
sentences.zh: 总的来说一切都好。

sentences.en: I just wish I could have a beer.
sentences.zh: 我只是希望能喝杯啤酒。

sentences.en: Right back.
sentences.zh: 回头见。

sentences.en: Love, Damien.
sentences.zh: 爱你的，达米安。

sentences.en: This is about a week before everything happened.
sentences.zh: 这大约是所有事情发生前一周的事。

sentences.en: And on a spring day, April 6, 2004, Damien Rodriguez takes a squad of about a dozen Marines out on a foot patrol.
sentences.zh: 在2004年4月6日的一个春天，达米安·罗德里格斯带着大约一打海军陆战队员的班进行徒步巡逻。

sentences.en: So we set out from the combat outpoSt. As we're moving through and leaving, we realize these streets that normally have kids throwing rocks at us, we're very empty.
sentences.zh: 于是我们从战斗前哨出发。当我们穿行离开时，我们发现这些平时总有小孩子向我们扔石头的街道非常空旷。

sentences.en: And this is about 11 a.m., something like that.
sentences.zh: 当时大约是上午11点左右，诸如此类的时间。

sentences.en: So that's strange.
sentences.zh: 所以这很奇怪。

sentences.en: Yeah, very strange.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常奇怪。

sentences.en: You always hear veterans, Vietnam vets, people like that say, you know it's going to be bad when it's quiet.
sentences.zh: 你经常听到老兵、越战老兵之类的人说，你知道当四周安静下来时情况就要不妙了。

sentences.en: What he didn't know is that there was this vast coordinated attack by insurgents about to happen citywide.
sentences.zh: 他不知道的是，叛乱分子即将全城爆发一场大规模的协同袭击。

sentences.en: And they round a corner walking down the sidewalk of an urban boulevard and fire just erupts from everywhere.
sentences.zh: 当他们转过街角、走在城市大道的人行道上时，枪声从四面八方突然爆发。

sentences.en: They opened up on us in a 360-degree ambush.
sentences.zh: 他们对我们发起了360度的伏击。

sentences.en: Windows, rooftops, alleys.
sentences.zh: 窗户、屋顶、小巷。

sentences.en: I can feel the rounds cracking around me.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到子弹在我身边呼啸而过。

sentences.en: I can feel in here.
sentences.zh: 我能在这里感觉到。

sentences.en: I can feel the air.
sentences.zh: 我能感受到空气。

sentences.en: I can feel, I can see them hitting all around me.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到，我能看到它们击中我周围的地面。

sentences.en: I felt and heard a really loud pop.
sentences.zh: 我感到并听到了一声非常响亮的爆裂声。

sentences.en: And then a very warm feeling all over my face because I was shot in the face right behind my right ear.
sentences.zh: 然后我整个脸都有一种非常温热的感觉，因为我的右耳下方中了一枪。

sentences.en: It severed the external carotid artery.
sentences.zh: 子弹切断了颈外动脉。

sentences.en: I should have been dead immediately.
sentences.zh: 我当时应该立刻就没命的。

sentences.en: It was pouring blood out.
sentences.zh: 血一直在喷涌而出。

sentences.en: Rodriguez takes the guys that he can get together and he holes up in a house and sort of tries to take stock.
sentences.zh: 罗德里格斯把能集结的人召集起来，躲进一所房子里，试图清点人数。

sentences.en: He's got two Marines already dead in the street and he can't get to the bodies because there's too much fire going on.
sentences.zh: 街上已经有两个海军陆战队员牺牲了，由于火力太猛，他无法靠近尸体。

sentences.en: Remember, he's in charge.
sentences.zh: 记住，他是负责人。

sentences.en: But at the same time, there's not a whole lot he can do.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他也无能为力。

sentences.en: They're running low on ammo.
sentences.zh: 他们的弹药快用光了。

sentences.en: He's got his hand pressed against the neck of another private who has been shot through the neck.
sentences.zh: 他用手紧紧按住另一个脖子中枪的二等兵的颈部。

sentences.en: And really, all he can do is keep shooting.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他能做的只有不断开枪还击。

sentences.en: He was cracking jokes with me, just trying to help me stay calm, which I was.
sentences.zh: 他当时还跟我开玩笑，试图帮我保持冷静，我也确实做到了。

sentences.en: And what kind of a joke could anyone, let alone your platoon leader, make at that moment to make you feel better when you've been shot in the face and you're bleeding like that?
sentences.zh: 当你脸部中枪、血流不止时，怎么会有人——更别提你的排长了——在那种时刻开玩笑来让你感觉好受点？

sentences.en: Well, there was a couple of them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时有好几个玩笑。

sentences.en: One of it was just, hey, you're going to be in Germany in no time hanging out with the nurses.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是，嘿，你很快就会去德国和护士们混在一起了。

sentences.en: What are you complaining about?
sentences.zh: 你还在抱怨什么？

sentences.en: You know, just give me a hard time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是故意找我茬。

sentences.en: And then they used to joke with me that I had a big nose and they said, hey, you just took a little bit off the tip, you know, stuff like that off the nose.
sentences.zh: 然后他们过去常开玩笑说我鼻子大，他们说，嘿，你刚才只是把鼻尖削掉了一点点，诸如此类关于鼻子的玩笑。

sentences.en: And so
sentences.zh: 所以

sentences.en: over the radio comes a report that, that the other group that was split off by them has just been hit by a grenade and they've got two guys down.
sentences.zh: 无线电里传来报告说，跟他们分开的另一组人刚刚遭到手榴弹袭击，有两个人倒下了。

sentences.en: They're still taking fire.
sentences.zh: 他们依然在遭受猛烈攻击。

sentences.en: He's called for reinforcements, but they can't get there because the whole city is essentially a repeat of this whole scene.
sentences.zh: 他请求了增援，但增援无法赶到，因为整个城市基本上都是这个场景的重演。

sentences.en: There's fighting going on all over the place.
sentences.zh: 到处都在发生战斗。

sentences.en: We finally were medevaced out of there, or I was.
sentences.zh: 我们最终被医疗直升机撤离了那里，或者说我被撤离了。

sentences.en: They showed up in the Humvees and he looked back at me and said, can you walk?
sentences.zh: 他们开着悍马车出现，他回头看着我问，你能走吗？

sentences.en: And I gave him a thumbs up, ran out there.
sentences.zh: 我朝他竖起大拇指，跑了过去。

sentences.en: He helped me get in the Humvee.
sentences.zh: 他帮我上了悍马车。

sentences.en: Marines are killed.
sentences.zh: 海军陆战队员牺牲了。

sentences.en: We've lost some of our friends or brothers.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了我们的一些朋友或兄弟。

sentences.en: There wasn't much of us left.
sentences.zh: 我们剩下的人已经不多了。

sentences.en: We're out of the city and sort of in a safe place.
sentences.zh: 我们离开了城市，到了一个相对安全的地方。

sentences.en: My platoon and I have just been relaxing, eating and exercising.
sentences.zh: 我和我的排刚刚一直在放松、吃东西和锻炼。

sentences.en: We've also been going to a lot of post-traumatic stress classes with the chaplains.
sentences.zh: 我们还一直在和牧师们一起参加许多创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的辅导课程。

sentences.en: It's one of those mandatory things, but it's good since my platoon have been through a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这是强制性要求的事项之一，但考虑到我的排经历了很多事情，这确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: Keep up the prayers for us and we should be home safe and sound.
sentences.zh: 请继续为我们祈祷，我们应该就能平平安安地回家了。

sentences.en: I look forward to seeing you.
sentences.zh: 我期待着见到你们。

sentences.en: Love, Damien.
sentences.zh: 爱你的，达米安。

sentences.en: Were you, when you got that note, Robbie, and he mentioned PTSD and what he and his fellow Marines had been through, were you worried about him?
sentences.zh: 罗比，当你收到那张便条，看到他提到PTSD以及他和队友们的经历时，你为他担心吗？

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: We were all worried.
sentences.zh: 我们都很担心。

sentences.en: We knew from the minute he came home because his eyes were,
sentences.zh: 从他回家的那一分钟起我们就知道了，因为他的眼神

sentences.en: I wouldn't say they're empty, but his eyes had changed.
sentences.zh: 我不会说那是空洞，但他的眼神变了。

sentences.en: When I looked into his eyes, there was just this like emptiness, just his body language and his spirit had been crushed.
sentences.zh: 当我看着他的眼睛时，只有那种空洞感，他的肢体语言和精神都已经被彻底击垮了。

sentences.en: That's how it felt.
sentences.zh: 当时给人的感觉就是这样。

sentences.en: Everyone I talked to sort of said the same thing, that after that first 2004 deployment, he was never really the same, he came home sullen.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的每个人几乎都说同样的话，在经历2004年的第一次部署之后，他整个人就彻底变了，回家后总是闷闷不乐。

sentences.en: He started drinking a lot more.
sentences.zh: 他开始大量酗酒。

sentences.en: He became
sentences.zh: 他变得

sentences.en: obsessed, isn't the right word, but consumed with the deaths of the men that, that had served under him.
sentences.zh: 执迷不悟——这个词或许不太准确，但他完全被那些曾在其手下服役却最终牺牲的战友的死给吞噬了。

sentences.en: I mean, every time we get together, he talks, he wants to talk to her.
sentences.zh: 我是说，每次我们聚在一起，他都在说，他总是想跟她聊起这些。

sentences.en: He wants to go through from the beginning of the patrol to all the way through it.
sentences.zh: 他想要从巡逻的起点一直讲到整个过程的结束。

sentences.en: He's sad.
sentences.zh: 他很难过。

sentences.en: I think he's sad a lot.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他有很长时间都非常难过。

sentences.en: He's hurting.
sentences.zh: 他在饱受折磨。

sentences.en: He was the platoon sergeant.
sentences.zh: 他当时是排长。

sentences.en: He was in charge, and his Marines were killed and were seriously wounded, and he thinks about it constantly.
sentences.zh: 他是负责人，而他的海军陆战队员们却牺牲了或身受重伤，他一直在脑海中反复回想这件事。

sentences.en: That's the way it changes you because it's never not on your mind.
sentences.zh: 这就是它改变你的方式，因为这永远会萦绕在你的心头。

sentences.en: When I first tried to talk to him about this, I flew out to his house.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次尝试跟他谈论这件事时，我坐飞机去了他家。

sentences.en: He lives near San Diego, and he had agreed to talk to me.
sentences.zh: 他住在圣迭戈附近，并且已经同意接受我的采访。

sentences.en: But this is something that is still so painful to him more than a decade later that he couldn't bring himself to come to the door.
sentences.zh: 但这件事情即使在十多年后对他的伤害依然如此之深，以至于他根本无法说服自己走到门前开门。

sentences.en: A few weeks later, after I think I gained a little more trust with him, he tried again.
sentences.zh: 几周后，我想我和他之间建立起了更多的信任，于是我们再次尝试。

sentences.en: We got on the phone,
sentences.zh: 我们通了电话，

sentences.en: and I asked him to take me back and just walk me through that scene from when the shooting started on the street.
sentences.zh: 我请他带我回到过去，把枪声从街头响起那一刻的场景重新梳理一遍。

sentences.en: And he tried.
sentences.zh: 而他尝试了。

sentences.en: He really tried.
sentences.zh: 他是真的很努力地去尝试了。

sentences.en: And he would start and pause and start and pause.
sentences.zh: 他总是讲讲停停，讲讲停停。

sentences.en: And then he just started crying, and he apologized, and he said he couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 然后他突然哭了起来，向我道歉，并说自己实在做不到。

sentences.en: I think that those images of seeing his Marines killed, being in charge, and not being able to do anything until it was too late, have never left him.
sentences.zh: 我想，那些目睹手下海军陆战队员阵亡的画面，那种身为负责人却无能为力直到为时已晚的愧疚，一直深深烙印在他心底。

sentences.en: But there's a lot that he doesn't remember.
sentences.zh: 但他也有很多记不清了。

sentences.en: He has a citation, a Bronze Star citation for valor that says that he killed 10 people that day.
sentences.zh: 他有一份紫星勋章的英勇表彰，上面说他在那天杀死了10个人。

sentences.en: And I asked him about that, and he said he couldn't remember it all clearly.
sentences.zh: 我向他问起这件事，而他说他已经记不清所有细节了。

sentences.en: And I know that the fact that there are people he killed that he can't really remember deeply bothers him.
sentences.zh: 我也知道，他亲手杀过人却又记不真切这个事实，深深地困扰着他。

sentences.en: You know, something so significant is kind of a blur.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如此重大的一段经历却变得有些模糊不清。

sentences.en: And you spend years trying to sort it out when it's not even clear in your mind and your memory what took place.
sentences.zh: 当你甚至无法在脑海和记忆中理清当时到底发生了什么时，你却要花上好几年的时间去试图解开这个心结。

sentences.en: Was he ever officially diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder?
sentences.zh: 他是否曾被正式诊断患有创伤后应激障碍？

sentences.en: After a couple of years, he was.
sentences.zh: 几年之后，是的。

sentences.en: He first started getting treated for what I think is pretty clearly typical symptoms of PTSD back in 2005, and in 2006, and in 2007.
sentences.zh: 早在2005年、2006年以及2007年，他就已经开始接受治疗，而这些治疗在我看来明显针对的是PTSD的典型症状。

sentences.en: He wasn't diagnosed until 2009.
sentences.zh: 直到2009年他才确诊。

sentences.en: And even then, I believe he kept it really quiet.
sentences.zh: 即便在那个时候，我也相信他一直把这事瞒得死死的。

sentences.en: There were treatments that were open to Marines,
sentences.zh: 海军陆战队确实有一些开放的治疗途径，

sentences.en: inpatient or intensive treatments where you could really sort of step aside and deal with this stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如住院治疗或强化治疗，你可以真正暂时脱离现实去处理这些问题。

sentences.en: And he chose not to do them because he was so afraid that if he did, his career was over.
sentences.zh: 但他选择不去，因为他太害怕了，生怕一旦去了自己的职业生涯就全毁了。

sentences.en: And when I say career, it's not just a career for a Marine like this.
sentences.zh: 当我说起职业生涯时，对这样一名海军陆战队员来说，这绝不仅仅是一份工作。

sentences.en: It's your entire life and identity.
sentences.zh: 这是你整个人生和身份认同。

sentences.en: It would have been taking everything that he thought he was and was most proud of and throwing it away.
sentences.zh: 这就等于把他自认为的全部以及他最为之自豪的一切统统抛弃掉。

sentences.en: So what kinds of things would put Damien on edge?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是什么样的事情会让达米安神经紧绷呢？

sentences.en: So this is really typical for anyone with this kind of war injury.
sentences.zh: 所以这对于任何受过这种战争创伤的人来说都非常典型。

sentences.en: They are hyper alert.
sentences.zh: 他们处于极度警觉状态。

sentences.en: If they go into an uncertain situation, it can be extremely uncomfortable for them.
sentences.zh: 如果他们进入一个充满不确定性的环境，会让他们感到极度不适。

sentences.en: So like the typical thing is a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 典型的例子就是餐馆。

sentences.en: You're in a room full of people you don't know.
sentences.zh: 你身处一个全是不认识之人的房间里。

sentences.en: Your back is to half of them.
sentences.zh: 你的后背对着其中一半的人。

sentences.en: And that can sort of ratchet up this sort of fear response.
sentences.zh: 这会成倍加剧这种恐惧反应。

sentences.en: And that was really typical for him for years after he got back from Iraq.
sentences.zh: 这正是他从伊拉克回来后多年里的典型状态。

sentences.en: And in fact, he would try to sit in a corner with his back to the wall if he could.
sentences.zh: 事实上，只要有可能，他总是尽量坐在角落里，把后背靠着墙。

sentences.en: And in fact, in the surveillance video at the Iraqi restaurant, what you see is that he's initially seated at a table in the middle of the room because it's busy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在伊拉克餐厅的监控视频中，你会发现他最初被安排坐在屋子正中间的一张桌子旁，因为当时店里人很多。

sentences.en: But as soon as the table opens up on the side of the room, he and his friend move over and he puts his back against the wall.
sentences.zh: 但一等餐厅靠墙的位子腾出来，他和朋友立刻就搬了过去，他把后背紧紧靠在了墙上。

sentences.en: Can you bring me up to the day of the alleged crime?
sentences.zh: 你能向我讲讲涉嫌犯罪的那天发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: What was Damien doing in Portland at that moment?
sentences.zh: 当时达米安在波特兰在做什么？

sentences.en: And what was going on in his life?
sentences.zh: 他的生活状况如何？

sentences.en: He had just been given a new assignment.
sentences.zh: 他刚刚接到了一项新任务。

sentences.en: It was going to be his last before he planned to retire.
sentences.zh: 这将是他计划退休前的最后一个任务。

sentences.en: He was taking over a little reserve unit in Portland.
sentences.zh: 他将在波特兰接管一个小型的预备役部队。

sentences.en: And after they had a little ceremony where he took command, he went out and celebrated.
sentences.zh: 在举行了一个小型的指挥权交接仪式后，他便出去庆祝了。

sentences.en: He went out with a Marine who he knew who lived in the area.
sentences.zh: 他和当地认识的一位海军陆战队战友一起出去了。

sentences.en: And they went to go to a bar on this artsy little street called Alberta Street up in northeast Portland.
sentences.zh: 他们打算去波特兰东北部一条充满艺术气息的小街——阿尔伯塔街上的一家酒吧。

sentences.en: And what's significant about this is
sentences.zh: 这里值得一提的是，

sentences.en: that it's April.
sentences.zh: 当时正值四月。

sentences.en: And April is the time when he is still dealing with the memories, the anniversary of this firefight that he hasn't gotten over.
sentences.zh: 而四月正是他依然沉浸在那些记忆中的时期，那场他至今仍未走出来的激烈交火的周年纪念日。

sentences.en: They go out drinking.
sentences.zh: 他们出去喝酒。

sentences.en: And they're actually on their way home from the bar when they walk past this Iraqi restaurant.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们正从酒吧走路回家，路过了这家伊拉克餐厅。

sentences.en: And both of them say, huh, we're kind of hungry.
sentences.zh: 两人都说，咦，我们有点饿了。

sentences.en: Iraq, that might be kind of cool.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克菜，听起来好像挺有意思的。

sentences.en: Let's go in and get something to eat.
sentences.zh: 进去吃点东西吧。

sentences.en: Surveillance video shows a man swinging a chair, attacking staff inside an Iraqi restaurant in northeast Portland.
sentences.zh: 监控视频显示，一名男子在波特兰东北部一家伊拉克餐馆内挥舞椅子，袭击店里的员工。

sentences.en: Turns out the man arrested and charged in this case is a U.S.
sentences.zh: 原来，在这起案件中被捕并被起诉的男子是一名美国

sentences.en: Marine and Iraq war veteran.
sentences.zh: 海军陆战队员及伊拉克战争老兵。

sentences.en: I guess the biggest problem with trying to deal with cases like this fairly is you never really know what was happening inside someone's head.
sentences.zh: 我想，公平处理这类案件最大的难题在于，你永远无法真正了解一个人脑子里在想什么。

sentences.en: Was he having a flashback or was he just angry over everything in his past and decided to hit somebody with a chair?
sentences.zh: 他当时是在经历闪回，还是只是对过去的种种感到愤怒，于是决定用椅子砸人？

sentences.en: I can't honestly say.
sentences.zh: 我老实说，我无法回答。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's it's pain is what that day was that night pain and alcohol.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是痛苦，那一天那个夜晚全是痛苦与酒精。

sentences.en: You can't take that one night and judge a man based off of that one night.
sentences.zh: 你不能单凭那一晚就给一个人定性。

sentences.en: It was a dumb mistake.
sentences.zh: 那只是个愚蠢的错误。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And he has to pay his consequences.
sentences.zh: 他也必须承担相应的后果。

sentences.en: I think they're being a little severe if you're asking my opinion, but being a little is an understatement.
sentences.zh: 如果要问我的意见，我觉得他们判得有点太重了，不过说“有点”还是太轻描淡写了。

sentences.en: Um, but he's, you know, he made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但他，你知道的，他犯了错。

sentences.en: He's paying for that mistake right now.
sentences.zh: 他现在正在为那个错误付出代价。

sentences.en: And, but do I think that he feels negatively towards Iraqis?
sentences.zh: 但是，你问我是否觉得他对伊拉克人抱有敌意？

sentences.en: No, we were there to, we gave our lives for that country.
sentences.zh: 并没有，我们当时去那里，我们为那个国家付出了生命。

sentences.en: We give our heart, our soul, everything for those people.
sentences.zh: 我们为那些人付出了我们的心、我们的灵魂，一切的一切。

sentences.en: The friends and family of this Marine would say that he did what he did in the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 这位海军陆战队员的朋友和家人会说，他在餐馆里的所作所为

sentences.en: They would say that he did that because of the trauma that he experienced.
sentences.zh: 他们会说他之所以那样做，是因为他所遭受的创伤。

sentences.en: What do you think about that explanation?
sentences.zh: 你对这种解释怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, I, I, you know, I, I, I really, I don't know him as a person, but I hear him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，你知道的，我，我，我真的，我不认识他的为人，但我能理解他。

sentences.en: I've been through the same.
sentences.zh: 我也经历过同样的遭遇。

sentences.en: My family been through the same.
sentences.zh: 我的家人也经历过同样的遭遇。

sentences.en: Most of Iraqi people been the same.
sentences.zh: 大多数伊拉克人民都经历过同样的遭遇。

sentences.en: Most of the American soldiers, Marines, they've been the same.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数美国士兵和海军陆战队员，也都经历过同样的遭遇。

sentences.en: So we share, but that's not something allowed me to go and, you know, and hit chairs, you know, for people I don't like.
sentences.zh: 所以我们感同身受，但这并不是我去袭击、去因为我不喜欢某些人而拿椅子砸人的借口。

sentences.en: It doesn't work this way.
sentences.zh: 事情不是这样的。

sentences.en: But you're saying you, you were both traumatized by the same war.
sentences.zh: 但你是说你，你们两人都被同一场战争所创伤。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I feel like,
sentences.zh: 我觉得，

sentences.en: I feel like really he needs help.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他真的很需要帮助。

sentences.en: I want people learn from the mistake.
sentences.zh: 我希望人们能从这个错误中吸取教训。

sentences.en: And if he, he said he did mistake and he did bad things and he will learn from it, I will forgive him.
sentences.zh: 如果他，如果他说他确实犯了错，做错了事，并且他会从中吸取教训，我会原谅他。

sentences.en: I, I really, I don't have any problem with him.
sentences.zh: 我，我真的，对他没有任何意见。

sentences.en: And, uh, and I wish all the best really for him.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，我是真心祝愿他一切都好。

sentences.en: And I feel if he can get help from his community, from his family, you know, and he learned about the forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果他能从他的社区、他的家人那里得到帮助，你知道的，并且他学会原谅。

sentences.en: And I think that would be the best way to make, you know, to make the world even more peaceful this way.
sentences.zh: 我想这将是让世界变得更加和平的最好方式。

sentences.en: Do you think that what he did was a hate crime?
sentences.zh: 你认为他的所作所为是一起仇恨犯罪吗？

sentences.en: I really, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我真的，我不知道。

sentences.en: I, I feel sorry for him.
sentences.zh: 我为他感到难过。

sentences.en: Believe me, you know, and I feel sorry for myself too.
sentences.zh: 相信我，你知道的，我也为自己感到难过。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be like this.
sentences.zh: 事情本不必是这样的。

sentences.en: It's really doesn't have to be like this.
sentences.zh: 事情真的本不必是这样的。

sentences.en: Hopefully he can get help.
sentences.zh: 希望他能得到帮助。

sentences.en: Dave, I would have imagined that the criminal justice system would account in some way for veterans, but here we're talking about Damien being charged with a hate crime.
sentences.zh: 戴夫，我本以为刑事司法系统会以某种方式照顾退伍军人，但在这里我们却看到达米安被控犯有仇恨犯罪。

sentences.en: Well, so all over the country, we've set up hundreds of what they call veterans treatment courts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以在全国各地，我们已经设立了数百个所谓的退伍军人治疗法院。

sentences.en: The idea being if you, if you get in trouble with the law and it has something to do with PTSD, we're going to give you a second chance.
sentences.zh: 其理念是，如果你因触犯法律而陷入麻烦，且这与PTSD有关，我们会给你第二次机会。

sentences.en: Instead of putting you behind bars, we're going to make sure that you get treatment because if we can straighten you out, you're good to go.
sentences.zh: 与其把你关进大牢，我们要确保你得到治疗，因为只要我们能帮你走上正轨，你就一切都好。

sentences.en: And we want to help you since, you know, you raised your hand and you served, you know, in the country's military.
sentences.zh: 既然你曾举手宣誓并在国家的军队中服役，你知道的，我们当然想帮你。

sentences.en: So Damien could be tried in one of these courts.
sentences.zh: 所以达米安本可以在这些法院里受审。

sentences.en: Well, that's the catch 22 is almost all of these courts won't allow veterans who are charged with a violent crime.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是两难的困境，几乎所有这些法院都不允许被控暴力犯罪的退伍军人进入。

sentences.en: Drug abuse, you bet.
sentences.zh: 吸毒，没问题。

sentences.en: Petty theft, sure.
sentences.zh: 小偷小摸，当然可以。

sentences.en: But putting a gun to someone's head or hitting somebody with a chair, well, then that gets into this really tough space of, okay, how much do we
sentences.zh: 但如果是拿枪指着别人的头或者用椅子砸人，那就进入了一个非常棘手的地带，即：我们究竟在多大程度上

sentences.en: give understanding and treatment to this person?
sentences.zh: 给予这个人理解和治疗？

sentences.en: And how much do we owe to the victim that's been harmed, you know?
sentences.zh: 而我们又在多大程度上亏欠了受到伤害的受害者呢？

sentences.en: And, and that's what we haven't worked out as a society.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们作为一个社会尚未理清的问题。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people have said to me, okay, so what?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很多人对我说过，那又怎样？

sentences.en: This guy was traumatized in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 这家伙在伊拉克受过创伤。

sentences.en: Think of all the people that are, are traumatized by a upbringing in a bad neighborhood or, or parents who are addicted to drugs.
sentences.zh: 想想看，有多少人在糟糕的街区环境中长大，或者父母酗酒吸毒，从而留下了心理创伤。

sentences.en: They don't get a special deal when they go into the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 当他们进入刑事司法系统时，并没有得到什么特殊照顾。

sentences.en: But I think it's really different because here's a person who's been injured by, uh, our federal policy, uh, injured
